senses.definition: To move or burst forth.
senses.example: The boat sprang a leak and began to sink.

senses.definition: To cause to spring (all senses).
To leap over.
senses.example: I sprang the fence, and was soon in the village street.

senses.definition: To breed with, to impregnate.
senses.example: ...[they] sought the fairest stoned horses to spring their mares...

senses.definition: To wet, to moisten.
To burst into pieces, to explode, to shatter.
senses.example: On the 22nd the mines sprang, and took very good effect.

senses.definition: To go off.
senses.example: The whole contraption appears liable to spring apart at any moment.

senses.definition: To crack.
senses.example: The Edward sprang hir foremast.

senses.definition: To come upon and flush out.
senses.example: For generations of men the springer spaniel has been looked upon as the dog for springing pheasants in covert and finding and retrieving dead birds or winged runners when ordered to do so. The properly broken dog will not chase, but drop to wing and shot.

senses.definition: To catch in an illegal act or compromising position.
senses.example: He figured that nobody would ever spring him, but he figured wrong.

senses.definition: To begin.
To put bad money into circulation.
To tell, to share.
senses.example: Sorry to spring it on you like this but I've been offered another job.

senses.definition: To free from imprisonment, especially by facilitating an illegal escape.
senses.example: His lieutenants hired a team of miners to help spring him.

senses.definition: To be free of imprisonment, especially by illegal escape.
To secure a person's release from custody; to free or bail out of jail.
senses.example: The Big Man, of course, had had an alibi as solid as Fort Knox. He had been held and questioned, but was quickly sprung by the best lawyer in Harlem.

senses.definition: To build, to form the initial curve of.
senses.example: They sprung an arch over the lintel.

senses.definition: To extend, to curve.
senses.example: The arches spring from the front posts.

senses.definition: To turn a vessel using a spring attached to its anchor cable.
To pay or spend a certain sum, to yield.
senses.example: He wouldn't spring a nickel for a bag of peanuts.

senses.definition: To raise an offered price.
Alternative form of sprain.
Alternative form of strain.
To act as a spring: to strongly rebound.
To equip with springs, especially (of vehicles) to equip with a suspension.
to inspire, to motivate.
To deform owing to excessive pressure, to become warped; to intentionally deform in order to position and then straighten in place.
senses.example: Don't drive it in too hard, as it will ‘spring’ the plane-iron, and make it concave.

senses.definition: To swell with milk or pregnancy.
senses.example:
“Gee, Dad, Nancy’s springing all right,” Ray said and paused in spontaneous pleasure.
Stan Parker came, and together they looked at their swelling heifer.

senses.definition: To sound, to play.
senses.example: I do not know how John and his mistress would have settled the fate of the thief, but just at this moment a policeman entered — for the cook had sprung the rattle, and had been screaming "Murder" and "Thieves."

senses.definition: To find or get enough food during springtime.
An act of springing: a leap, a jump.
The season of the year in temperate regions in which temperatures and daylight hours rise, and plants spring from the ground and into bloom and dormant animals spring to life.
senses.example: Spring is the time of the year most species reproduce.

senses.definition: The time of something's growth; the early stages of some process.
senses.example: ...and it came to passe about the spring of the day, that Samuel called Saul to the top of the house...

senses.definition: Someone with ivory or peach skin tone and eyes and hair that are not extremely dark, seen as best suited to certain colors of clothing.
Something which springs, springs forth, springs up, or springs back, particularly
senses.example: This beer was brewed with pure spring water.

senses.definition: An erection of the penis.
A crack which has sprung up in a mast, spar, or (rare) a plank or seam.
senses.example: A spar is said to be sprung, when it is cracked or split,... and the crack is called a spring.

senses.definition: Springiness: an attribute or quality of springing, springing up, or springing back, particularly
senses.example: the spring of a bow

senses.definition: The source from which an action or supply of something springs.
senses.example: As wel the singers as the players on instruments shall bee there: all my springs are in thee.

senses.definition: Something which causes others or another to spring forth or spring into action, particularly
senses.example: Our Author ſhuns by vulgar Springs to move / The Hero's Glory, or the Virgin's Love; […]

senses.definition: To spend the springtime somewhere.
senses.example: True it is that, owing to the migratory propensities of our countrymen, every third man has wintered at Naples, springed at Vienna, summered in Switzerland, and autumned on the banks of the Lago Maggiore;

senses.definition: A surname.
A census-designated place in Harris County, Texas, United States.
Alternative form of spring, the season of warmth and new vegetation following winter.
senses.example: There the roſy-finger'd Spring, by the liquid mirror of a cryſtalline pool, was attiring her fair daughters in ſeven-fold ornaments, while the love-whiſpering breezes ſtole kiſſes as they paſſed, and fanned their glowing beauties.
